objects.description: C++ wrapper class for the C libmosquitto client (struct mosquitto). It owns an internal struct mosquitto* (m_mosq) and exposes most client operations (connect, publish, subscribe, loop, TLS setup, etc.) plus virtual callbacks to be overridden by users. Constructed with an optional client id and clean-session flag; destroyed via virtual destructor which cleans up the underlying C client. All other free-standing functions in this header are declarations only and belong to the mosqpp namespace.

functions.name: mosqpp::strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing a libmosquitto error code. C++ wrapper of mosquitto_strerror.
requirements: mosq_errno must be a valid mosq_err_t error code, otherwise a generic/unknown string may be returned.

functions.name: mosqpp::connack_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for an MQTT v3.x CONNACK return code. C++ wrapper of mosquitto_connack_string.
requirements: connack_code should be a valid mqtt311_connack_codes value.

functions.name: mosqpp::sub_topic_tokenise
functions.signature: mosqpp_EXPORT int mosqpp::sub_topic_tokenise(const char *subtopic, char ***topics, int *count);
functions.description: Tokenises a topic/subscription string into an array of hierarchy components. Wrapper of mosquitto_sub_topic_tokenise.
requirements: subtopic must be valid UTF-8.
topics must be non-NULL and will receive an allocated array; free with mosqpp::sub_topic_tokens_free.
count must be non-NULL and will be set to the number of tokens.

functions.name: mosqpp::sub_topic_tokens_free
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by sub_topic_tokenise. Wrapper of mosquitto_sub_topic_tokens_free.
requirements: topics must be a pointer to the array returned by sub_topic_tokenise.
count must match the number of tokens originally returned.

functions.name: mosqpp::lib_version
functions.description: Retrieves libmosquitto version numbers (major, minor, revision). Wrapper of mosquitto_lib_version. Returns a combined integer LIBMOSQUITTO_VERSION_NUMBER.
requirements: major, minor, revision may be NULL individually; non-NULL pointers will be written.

functions.name: mosqpp::lib_init
functions.description: Initialises the libmosquitto library. Must be called before other mosquitto operations if using the C API directly. Wrapper of mosquitto_lib_init.
requirements: Not thread safe; must not be called concurrently.
Should be paired with mosqpp::lib_cleanup when done.

functions.name: mosqpp::lib_cleanup
functions.description: Cleans up resources associated with libmosquitto. Wrapper of mosquitto_lib_cleanup.
requirements: Call after finishing with the library (pairs with lib_init).
Must not be called concurrently with other mosquitto operations.

functions.name: mosqpp::topic_matches_sub
functions.signature: mosqpp_EXPORT int mosqpp::topic_matches_sub(const char *sub, const char *topic, bool *result);
functions.description: Checks whether a topic matches a given subscription pattern (supports + and # wildcards). Wrapper of mosquitto_topic_matches_sub.
requirements: sub must be a valid subscription string (valid UTF-8).
topic must be a valid topic string (valid UTF-8).
result must be non-NULL to receive true/false.

functions.name: mosqpp::validate_utf8
functions.signature: mosqpp_EXPORT int mosqpp::validate_utf8(const char *str, int len);
functions.description: Validates that a string is valid UTF-8 per MQTT rules. Wrapper of mosquitto_validate_utf8.
requirements: If str is NULL, len must be 0.
len must be >=0 and <=65536.

functions.name: mosqpp::subscribe_simple
functions.signature: mosqpp_EXPORT int mosqpp::subscribe_simple(struct mosquitto_message **messages, int msg_count, bool retained, const char *topic, int qos=0, const char *host="localhost", int port=1883, const char *client_id=NULL, int keepalive=60, bool clean_session=true, const char *username=NULL, const char *password=NULL, const struct libmosquitto_will *will=NULL, const struct libmosquitto_tls *tls=NULL);
functions.description: Helper to connect to a broker, subscribe to a topic, collect msg_count messages, then disconnect. Wrapper of mosquitto_subscribe_simple.
requirements: messages must be a pointer to a struct mosquitto_message*; on success it will be set to an allocated array of messages that the caller must free with mosquitto_message_free for each plus array memory per implementation.
msg_count must be > 0.
topic must be a valid subscription string (UTF-8).
qos must be 0, 1, or 2.
If username is NULL, password is ignored.
If tls is provided, its members must be valid for TLS configuration.
If will is provided, its fields must satisfy will constraints (topic valid UTF-8; payloadlen within MQTT limits).

functions.name: mosqpp::subscribe_callback
functions.signature: mosqpp_EXPORT int mosqpp::subscribe_callback(int (*callback)(struct mosquitto *, void *, const struct mosquitto_message *), void *userdata, const char *topic, int qos=0, const char *host="localhost", int port=1883, const char *client_id=NULL, int keepalive=60, bool clean_session=true, const char *username=NULL, const char *password=NULL, const struct libmosquitto_will *will=NULL, const struct libmosquitto_tls *tls=NULL);
functions.description: Helper to connect to a broker, subscribe to a topic, and invoke a user callback for received messages; returns after the callback returns 1, then disconnects. Wrapper of mosquitto_subscribe_callback.
requirements: callback must be non-NULL and must return 1 to stop processing, otherwise continue.
topic must be a valid subscription string (UTF-8).
qos must be 0, 1, or 2.
userdata is passed to the callback as its obj parameter.
If username is NULL, password is ignored.
If tls is provided, its members must be valid for TLS configuration.
If will is provided, its fields must satisfy will constraints (topic valid UTF-8; payloadlen within MQTT limits).

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::mosquittopp
functions.description: Constructs a C++ MQTT client wrapper around libmosquitto with an optional client id and clean session flag.
requirements: If id is NULL, clean_session must be true (per MQTT 3.x rules).
If id is not NULL, it must be valid UTF-8 and within broker limits.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::~mosquittopp
functions.description: Destructor for the C++ MQTT client wrapper; frees associated resources and any underlying libmosquitto instance.
requirements: Do not use the instance after destruction.
Ensure any running loop thread has been stopped before object destruction to avoid races.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::reinitialise
functions.description: Reinitialises the client instance with a new client id and clean session setting; analogous to mosquitto_reinitialise.
requirements: Must be called on a valid mosquittopp instance.
If id is NULL, clean_session must be true.
If connected, this will close any open network connections as part of reinitialisation.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::socket
functions.description: Returns the network socket descriptor for this client; analogous to mosquitto_socket.
requirements: Only valid after initialisation; returns -1 on failure.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::will_set
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::will_set(const char *topic, int payloadlen=0, const void *payload=NULL, int qos=0, bool retain=false);
functions.description: Configures the client Last Will and Testament (LWT). Must be called before connect. Wraps mosquitto_will_set.
requirements: Must be called before any connect/connect_async call.
topic must be valid UTF-8.
payloadlen must be between 0 and 268,435,455 inclusive; if >0, payload must be a valid pointer.
qos must be 0, 1, or 2.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::will_clear
functions.description: Clears any previously configured LWT. Must be called before connect. Wraps mosquitto_will_clear.
requirements: Call before connecting (connect/connect_async).

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::username_pw_set
functions.description: Sets username and password for broker authentication. Must be called before connect. Wraps mosquitto_username_pw_set.
requirements: Call before connecting.
If username is NULL, password is ignored.
Strings must remain valid until connect is called or copied internally by the library.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::connect
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::connect(const char *host, int port=1883, int keepalive=60);
functions.description: Connects to a broker (blocking semantics as per mosquitto_connect).
requirements: host must be non-NULL.
port must be >= 0.
keepalive must be >= 5 (or 0 for infinite).
Ensure network loop is serviced (loop/loop_start) to complete network I/O.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::connect_async
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::connect_async(const char *host, int port=1883, int keepalive=60);
functions.description: Initiates a non-blocking connection to a broker. Requires using the threaded loop (loop_start). Wraps mosquitto_connect_async.
requirements: host must be non-NULL.
port must be >= 0.
keepalive must be >= 5 (or 0 for infinite).
If using connect_async, use loop_start (threaded interface).

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::reconnect
functions.description: Reconnects to the broker using previous connection parameters. Wraps mosquitto_reconnect.
requirements: Must only be called after an initial connect/connect_async has been made.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::reconnect_async
functions.description: Non-blocking reconnect using previous parameters. Wraps mosquitto_reconnect_async.
requirements: Must only be called after an initial connect/connect_async has been made.
Use the threaded loop interface (loop_start) for async operation.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::disconnect
functions.description: Disconnects from the broker. Wraps mosquitto_disconnect.
requirements: Client should be connected; returns error if no connection.
Ensure loop is serviced so the DISCONNECT is actually sent (important if a Will is set).

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::publish
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::publish(int *mid, const char *topic, int payloadlen=0, const void *payload=NULL, int qos=0, bool retain=false);
functions.description: Publishes a message to a topic. Wraps mosquitto_publish.
requirements: Client must be connected to publish successfully.
topic must be valid UTF-8 and a publish topic (no wildcards).
payloadlen must be between 0 and 268,435,455 inclusive; if >0, payload must be a valid pointer.
qos must be 0, 1, or 2.
If mid is non-NULL, it will be set to the message id.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::subscribe
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::subscribe(int *mid, const char *sub, int qos=0);
functions.description: Subscribes to a topic filter. Wraps mosquitto_subscribe.
requirements: Client must be connected.
sub must be a valid subscription string (valid UTF-8; wildcards in valid positions).
qos must be 0, 1, or 2.
If mid is non-NULL, it will be set to the message id.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::unsubscribe
functions.description: Unsubscribes from a topic filter. Wraps mosquitto_unsubscribe.
requirements: Client must be connected.
sub must be valid UTF-8.
If mid is non-NULL, it will be set to the message id.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::reconnect_delay_set
functions.signature: void mosqpp::mosquittopp::reconnect_delay_set(unsigned int reconnect_delay, unsigned int reconnect_delay_max, bool reconnect_exponential_backoff);
functions.description: Configures reconnect delay behavior for automatic reconnection in loop_forever/loop_start. Wraps mosquitto_reconnect_delay_set.
requirements: reconnect_delay and reconnect_delay_max are in seconds; max should be >= delay.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::max_inflight_messages_set
functions.description: Sets maximum number of in-flight QoS 1/2 messages (deprecated in favor of MOSQ_OPT_SEND_MAXIMUM). Wraps mosquitto_max_inflight_messages_set.
requirements: max_inflight_messages >= 0 (0 means no maximum).

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::message_retry_set
functions.description: No-op in current library versions. Retained for API compatibility. Wraps mosquitto_message_retry_set.
requirements: No specific requirements; function has no effect.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::user_data_set
functions.description: Sets/updates the user data pointer associated with callbacks. Wraps mosquitto_user_data_set.
requirements: userdata can be NULL; the pointer is stored as-is. Caller is responsible for managing its lifetime.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::tls_set
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::tls_set(const char *cafile, const char *capath=NULL, const char *certfile=NULL, const char *keyfile=NULL, int (*pw_callback)(char *buf, int size, int rwflag, void *userdata)=NULL);
functions.description: Configures certificate-based TLS. Must be called before connecting. Wraps mosquitto_tls_set.
requirements: Call before connect/connect_async.
At least one of cafile or capath must be non-NULL.
If certfile is NULL, keyfile must also be NULL (no client cert).
If keyfile is NULL, certfile must also be NULL.
If keyfile is encrypted, provide pw_callback or be prepared for interactive password entry.
Using TLS implies valid file paths and appropriate OpenSSL configuration.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::tls_opts_set
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::tls_opts_set(int cert_reqs, const char *tls_version=NULL, const char *ciphers=NULL);
functions.description: Sets advanced TLS options such as verification requirements, protocol version, and ciphers. Must be called before connecting. Wraps mosquitto_tls_opts_set.
requirements: Call before connect/connect_async.
cert_reqs should be SSL_VERIFY_NONE (0) or SSL_VERIFY_PEER (1).
tls_version may be NULL or one of supported strings (e.g., "tlsv1.2").
ciphers may be NULL to use defaults.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::tls_insecure_set
functions.description: Enables/disables TLS hostname verification. Must be called before connecting. Wraps mosquitto_tls_insecure_set.
requirements: Call before connect/connect_async.
Setting value=true disables hostname checking and is insecure; use only for testing.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::tls_psk_set
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::tls_psk_set(const char *psk, const char *identity, const char *ciphers=NULL);
functions.description: Configures PSK-based TLS. Must be called before connecting. Wraps mosquitto_tls_psk_set.
requirements: Call before connect/connect_async.
psk must be a hex string with no leading 0x.
identity must be non-NULL.
Cannot be used together with certificate-based TLS (tls_set).
ciphers may be NULL to use defaults.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::opts_set
functions.description: Deprecated generic option setter. Prefer mosquitto_int_option/string_option/void_option. Wraps mosquitto_opts_set.
requirements: option must be a valid mosq_opt_t.
value type/meaning depends on option; must match expected type.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::loop
functions.description: Drives the client's network I/O once; should be called frequently if not using the threaded helper. Wraps mosquitto_loop.
requirements: Must not be called from within a callback.
timeout < 0 uses default (1000ms); 0 returns immediately; >0 waits up to that many ms.
max_packets currently unused; set to 1 for compatibility.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::loop_misc
functions.description: Performs miscellaneous periodic tasks (PING handling, retry checks). Use when integrating into your own event loop. Wraps mosquitto_loop_misc.
requirements: Call approximately once per second if you manage your own select/poll loop.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::loop_read
functions.description: Performs network read operations; for custom event-loop integrations. Wraps mosquitto_loop_read.
requirements: Use only if not using loop().
Client must be connected or connecting.
max_packets currently unused; set to 1 for compatibility.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::loop_write
functions.description: Performs network write operations; for custom event-loop integrations. Wraps mosquitto_loop_write.
requirements: Use only if not using loop().
Client must be connected or connecting.
max_packets currently unused; set to 1 for compatibility.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::loop_forever
functions.description: Runs the network loop in a blocking fashion, handling reconnects automatically. Returns when disconnects cleanly or on error. Wraps mosquitto_loop_forever.
requirements: Not to be used if you need your thread for other tasks (it blocks).
timeout semantics as per loop().
max_packets currently unused; set to 1 for compatibility.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::loop_start
functions.description: Starts a background thread to run the network loop. Wraps mosquitto_loop_start.
requirements: Thread support must be available.
Call once per client.
Pair with loop_stop() to stop the thread.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::loop_stop
functions.description: Stops the background network loop thread started by loop_start. Blocks until the thread exits. Wraps mosquitto_loop_stop.
requirements: Call only after loop_start().
If force is false, mosquitto_disconnect should have been called to allow thread to end; set force=true to cancel.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::want_write
functions.description: Returns whether there is data pending to write on the socket. Wraps mosquitto_want_write.
requirements: Client must be initialised. Used for custom event loops alongside socket().

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::threaded_set
functions.description: Informs the library that the application uses threads but not loop_start, to avoid single-thread optimisations that could cause race conditions. Wraps mosquitto_threaded_set.
requirements: Call this if you manage your own threads and do not use loop_start().

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::socks5_set
functions.signature: int mosqpp::mosquittopp::socks5_set(const char *host, int port=1080, const char *username=NULL, const char *password=NULL);
functions.description: Configures use of a SOCKS5 proxy for subsequent connections. Wraps mosquitto_socks5_set.
requirements: Call before connect/connect_async.
host must be non-NULL.
port must be valid for SOCKS5 (typically 1–65535).
If username is NULL, password is ignored.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_connect
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked when a CONNACK is received after connecting.
requirements: No explicit requirements documented in header. Typical guidance: keep callbacks non-blocking and thread-safe.
Do not call loop() from inside callbacks (per libmosquitto guidance).

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_connect_with_flags
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked on connect with additional flags indicating broker/session info.
requirements: No explicit requirements documented in header. Keep callback lightweight and thread-safe.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_disconnect
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked when the client disconnects from the broker.
requirements: No explicit requirements documented in header. Keep callback lightweight and thread-safe.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_publish
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked when a message initiated with publish has completed per its QoS.
requirements: No explicit requirements documented in header. mid corresponds to the message id provided/assigned.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_message
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked when a message is received and QoS flow has completed.
requirements: message pointer is only valid for the duration of the callback; copy data if needed afterward (per libmosquitto semantics).
Keep callback lightweight and thread-safe.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_subscribe
functions.signature: virtual void mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_subscribe(int mid, int qos_count, const int *granted_qos);
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked when a SUBACK is received in response to subscribe.
requirements: granted_qos points to an array of qos_count integers valid during the callback.
Keep callback lightweight and thread-safe.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_unsubscribe
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked when an UNSUBACK is received in response to unsubscribe.
requirements: Keep callback lightweight and thread-safe.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_log
functions.signature: virtual void mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_log(int level, const char *str);
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked for client library log messages.
requirements: level is a bitmask of MOSQ_LOG_* flags; str is a C-string valid during the callback.
Keep callback lightweight and thread-safe.

functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::on_error
functions.description: User-overridable callback invoked on client error conditions (C++ wrapper convenience).
requirements: No explicit requirements documented in header. Keep callback lightweight and thread-safe.

unharnessable_functions.name: mosqpp::subscribe_simple
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires real network connectivity to an MQTT broker and may block, which is unsuitable for the fuzzer runtime.

unharnessable_functions.name: mosqpp::subscribe_callback
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on asynchronous network I/O and user callback invocation against a real broker, which is unsuitable for the fuzzer runtime.

unharnessable_functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::connect
unharnessable_functions.reason: Performs blocking network operations to connect to a broker and may stall or depend on external environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::connect_async
unharnessable_functions.reason: Initiates network operations and requires threaded loop handling against a broker, which is not suitable for deterministic fuzzing without external dependencies.

unharnessable_functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::opts_set
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires specific enum option values with correctly typed void* payloads that cannot be safely provided without the full enum/type context.

unharnessable_functions.name: mosqpp::mosquittopp::loop_forever
unharnessable_functions.reason: It blocks the calling thread by design, which would hang the fuzzer runtime.

data_types.description: A byte sequence that is valid UTF-8 text. May contain any Unicode code points permitted by UTF-8 encoding. Used wherever the API requires MQTT-valid UTF-8 strings (topics, client IDs, identities, messages).
Arbitrary bytes with no required encoding or structure. May include NULs and any 8-bit values. Used for payload buffers and generic data validation where length is supplied separately.

A string representing a path to a file on the local filesystem. Used to locate files that will be read by the library (e.g., CA file, certificate/key files, or a directory path). The content of the file is what the target ultimately consumes.

A textual string intended to be simple printable ASCII (not strictly enforced by the stub) such as TLS version labels (e.g., "tlsv1.2") or cipher suite lists. Typically short and without Unicode requirements.
A string consisting solely of hexadecimal digits 0-9 and a-f (lowercase in this stub), with even length, representing binary data such as a PSK key. No leading 0x prefix.
A network host identifier such as a DNS name or IPv4/IPv6 literal presented as a string. Used where a server or proxy host must be specified.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import itertools

# This generator produces valid UTF-8 strings suitable for MQTT/libmosquitto contexts.
# It focuses on topics, subscriptions, client IDs, identities, PSK ciphers strings, etc.
# We pack multiple UTF-8 strings and some integers into one buffer; the fuzzer splits
# these via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) in the target stubs.
#
# Strategy
# - Emit a sequence of UTF-8 strings covering different MQTT topic/subscription patterns
#   (wildcards + and # in legal positions), normal publish topics (no wildcards),
#   client IDs (ASCII and Unicode), and generic short strings.
# - Interleave unsigned ints to drive options like qos/retain/mid/ciphers-choice/ports.
# - Keep overall size <= 4096 bytes.
# - All strings are valid UTF-8 and within the size limits enforced by the stubs.
#
# Encoding format consumed by the fuzzer harness:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR: harness extracts length-prefixed or NUL-terminated segments depending
#   on its implementation. Since we don't control that here, we output multiple strings
#   separated by '\n' (newline) and also include length-prefixed blocks to increase the
#   chance of correct parsing. This tends to work with common fuzzing harnesses that slice
#   by delimiters or lengths. Integers are emitted in little-endian 4-byte chunks and
#   can be read by FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int).
#
# Note: The fuzzer stubs validate UTF-8 using mosqpp::validate_utf8, so we ensure validity.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII = [
    "",
    "a",
    "test",
    "mqtt",
    "client",
    "user",
    "password",
    "localhost",
]

# Some Unicode snippets (valid UTF-8), avoiding surrogates
UNICODE = [
    "αβγ",
    "日本語",
    "emoji-🙂",
    "🌐mqtt",
    "тест",
    "موزوع",
    "καλημέρα",
]

# Subscription patterns (valid positions for + and #)
SUB_PATTERNS = [
    "+",
    "#",
    "+/sensor",
    "home/+/temp",
    "home/#",
    "devices/+/status/+",
    "a/b/c",
    "室内/+/温度",
]

# Publish topics (must not contain wildcards)
PUB_TOPICS = [
    "home/kitchen/temp",
    "sensors/room1/humidity",
    "devices/123/status",
    "室内/温度",
    "emoji/🙂/value",
]

# Client IDs typical max 23 chars
CLIENT_IDS = [
    "client-" + str(i) for i in range(1, 6)
] + [
    "cid-🙂",
    "αβγ-123",
]

# Cipher names examples (OpenSSL-like token strings)
CIPHERS = [
    "DEFAULT",
    "HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5",
    "TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256",
    "TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256",
]


def _rand_choice(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_utf8(rng, max_len):
    # Build a random valid UTF-8 string from pools
    pools = [ASCII, UNICODE]
    parts = []
    while len("".join(parts)) < max_len and rng.random() < 0.85:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, _rand_choice(rng, pools))
        parts.append(s)
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append("/")  # useful for topics
    s = "".join(parts)
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s


def _emit_str(buf, s):
    # Append as: length (LE uint16) + bytes + newline form as well
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    ln = min(len(b), 1024)
    b = b[:ln]
    buf.append(struct.pack('<H', len(b)))
    buf.append(b)
    buf.append(b"\n")


def _emit_uint(buf, val):
    buf.append(struct.pack('<I', val & 0xFFFFFFFF))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = []

    # 1) Strings for sub_topic_tokenise and topic_matches_sub
    # Mix subscription filters and topics; ensure valid UTF-8 and bounded sizes
    sub = _rand_choice(rng, SUB_PATTERNS)
    topic = _rand_choice(rng, PUB_TOPICS)
    _emit_str(out, sub[:256])
    _emit_str(out, topic[:256])

    # Another pair to give more chances to the harness
    _emit_str(out, _rand_choice(rng, SUB_PATTERNS)[:256])
    _emit_str(out, _rand_choice(rng, PUB_TOPICS)[:256])

    # 2) Constructor id and clean_session chooser via integer pick
    # pick bits: bit0->use_null_id, bit1->clean_session when id given
    pick = 0
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pick |= 1  # use NULL id
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pick |= 2  # clean session when id non-NULL
    _emit_uint(out, pick)

    # If non-NULL id path is taken by harness sometimes, provide a valid id string
    cid = _rand_choice(rng, CLIENT_IDS)
    if len(cid) > 23:
        cid = cid[:23]
    _emit_str(out, cid)

    # 3) Reinitialise picks
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))
    _emit_str(out, _rand_choice(rng, CLIENT_IDS)[:23])

    # 4) Will parameters: topic, payload, payloadlen, qos, retain
    _emit_str(out, _rand_choice(rng, PUB_TOPICS)[:256])
    payload = _rand_utf8(rng, 512)
    _emit_str(out, payload)
    # payloadlen chooses within payload size
    payload_len_pick = rng.randrange(len(payload.encode('utf-8')) + 1) if payload else 0
    _emit_uint(out, payload_len_pick)
    _emit_uint(out, rng.randrange(3))  # qos 0..2
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # retain flag via bit

    # 5) Username/password set; pick controls NULL/non-NULL
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))
    _emit_str(out, _rand_utf8(rng, 64))  # username
    _emit_str(out, _rand_utf8(rng, 64))  # password

    # 6) Publish parameters
    _emit_str(out, _rand_choice(rng, PUB_TOPICS)[:128])  # topic
    pub_payload = _rand_utf8(rng, 1024)
    _emit_str(out, pub_payload)
    _emit_uint(out, rng.randrange(len(pub_payload.encode('utf-8')) + 1 if pub_payload else 1))  # payloadlen
    _emit_uint(out, rng.randrange(3))  # qos
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # retain flag bit
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # decide mid_ptr null/non-null

    # 7) Subscribe parameters
    _emit_str(out, _rand_choice(rng, SUB_PATTERNS)[:128])
    _emit_uint(out, rng.randrange(3))  # qos
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # decide mid_ptr

    # 8) Unsubscribe parameters
    _emit_str(out, _rand_choice(rng, SUB_PATTERNS)[:128])
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))

    # 9) TLS PSK set: nbytes and hex string are constructed in stub using FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int),
    #    but we only influence via RNG picks; provide identity and optional ciphers chooser.
    #    We add multiple uints for randomness, identity, ciphers candidate.
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # nbytes chooser
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # hex digits chooser stream
    _emit_str(out, _rand_utf8(rng, 32))   # identity (<=64 in stub)
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # whether to include ciphers
    _emit_str(out, _rand_choice(rng, CIPHERS)[:32])

    # 10) SOCKS5 set: host, port, creds optional
    _emit_str(out, (_rand_utf8(rng, 16) or "localhost")[:128])
    _emit_uint(out, rng.randrange(1, 65536))  # port 1..65535
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # pick for creds on/off
    _emit_str(out, _rand_utf8(rng, 32))  # username
    _emit_str(out, _rand_utf8(rng, 32))  # password

    # 11) on_log: level and message
    _emit_uint(out, rng.getrandbits(32))  # level bitmask
    _emit_str(out, _rand_utf8(rng, 128))

    data = b"".join(out)
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data

import random
import struct

# This generator provides length-prefixed strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers in mosquittopp tests.
# Focus on valid UTF-8 topics and diverse payloads within bounds; buffer <= 4096 bytes.


def _lp(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(b) > 65535:
        b = b[:65535]
    return struct.pack('>H', len(b)) + b


def _topic_segments(r: random.Random) -> list:
    alph = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-.'
    segs = []
    n = r.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(n):
        seg_len = r.randint(1, 20)
        s = ''.join(r.choice(alph) for _ in range(seg_len))
        segs.append(s)
    return segs


def _utf8_mix(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    if max_len <= 0:
        return ''
    parts = []
    # Build up until reaching byte budget
    while True:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.7:
            parts.append(chr(r.randint(0x20, 0x7E)))
        elif choice < 0.9:
            parts.append(chr(r.choice(list(range(0x00A1, 0x00FF)))))
        else:
            parts.append(r.choice(['Ω', 'Ж', '中', '漢', '🙂', '✓', '€', '®', '™']))
        b = ''.join(parts).encode('utf-8')
        if len(b) >= max_len:
            break
        if len(parts) > max_len:  # safeguard
            break
    return ''.join(parts)[:max_len]


def _binary_payload(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    max_len = max(0, int(max_len))
    if max_len == 0:
        return b''
    patterns = []
    # Repeating patterns
    base = r.choice([b'\x00', b'\xff', b'AB', b'\x00\xff', b'1234'])
    # Ensure multiplier range is valid
    mult_max = max_len // max(1, len(base))
    if mult_max <= 0:
        rep = base[:max_len]
    else:
        rep = base * r.randint(1, mult_max)
        rep = rep[:max_len]
    patterns.append(rep)
    # Random bytes
    patterns.append(bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(r.randint(0, max_len))))
    # ASCII text
    text_chars = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-:/.,\n\r\t"
    patterns.append(bytes(r.choice(text_chars) for _ in range(r.randint(0, max_len))))
    # Mixed sequence
    mix = bytearray()
    parts = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(parts):
        seg_len = r.randint(0, max(0, max_len // 4))
        if seg_len:
            mix.extend(bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(seg_len)))
        mix.extend(r.choice([b'\x00', b'\xff', b'']))
    patterns.append(bytes(mix[:max_len]))
    return r.choice(patterns)[:max_len]


def _build_strings(r: random.Random) -> list:
    strings: list[bytes] = []

    # 1) validate_utf8-related
    strings.append(b"")
    strings.append(b"a")
    strings.append("caf\u00e9".encode('utf-8'))
    strings.append("hello/there".encode('utf-8'))
    s_mix = _utf8_mix(r, 200)
    strings.append(s_mix.encode('utf-8'))

    # 2) Publish topics (<=128 bytes)
    for _ in range(5):
        segs = _topic_segments(r)
        topic = '/'.join(s.strip('/') for s in segs)
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            topic = '/' + topic
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            topic = topic + '/'
        strings.append(topic.encode('utf-8')[:128])

    # 3) Subscription-like strings
    for s in ["+/sensor/+/temp", "devices/+/status", "building/room/#", "#", "+"]:
        strings.append(s.encode('utf-8'))

    # 4) Payloads up to 1024 bytes
    for _ in range(8):
        plen = r.randint(0, 1024)
        strings.append(_binary_payload(r, plen))

    # 5) Boundary UTF-8 sizes
    for bound in (64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512):
        s = _utf8_mix(r, bound)
        strings.append(s.encode('utf-8')[:bound])

    # 6) Small payloads
    strings.extend([b"", b"0", b"true", b"false", b"retain", b"qos0", b"qos1", b"qos2"])

    return [s[:1024] for s in strings]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    parts: list[bytes] = []

    strings = _build_strings(r)

    magic = b"MQTTSEED\x01"
    count = len(strings)
    parts.append(magic)
    parts.append(struct.pack('>H', count if count <= 0xFFFF else 0xFFFF))

    total = len(magic) + 2
    for s in strings:
        chunk = _lp(s)
        if total + len(chunk) > 4096:
            break
        parts.append(chunk)
        total += len(chunk)

    return b"".join(parts)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for files and directories used by mosqpp::mosquittopp::tls_set fuzz stub.
# FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() will return a path pointing to random fuzzable data.
# We create a small virtual filesystem layout in a single bytes buffer that the
# harness can map to files. The layout encodes multiple files and one directory
# with plausible TLS materials:
#  - CA certificate file (PEM)
#  - CA directory (capath) with hashed symlink-like entries
#  - Client certificate (PEM)
#  - Client private key (PKCS#8 PEM or traditional PEM)
#  - Also include some variations (short cert, multiple cert chain, encrypted key header)
#
# Buffer format we emit (simple TLV style):
#  magic: 4 bytes: b'MFS1'
#  entry_count: u16
#  For each entry:
#    type: u8 (0=file, 1=dir)
#    path_len: u16
#    path: bytes (UTF-8)
#    content_len: u32 (for file) or 0 for dir
#    content: bytes (for file)
#
# The fuzzing harness should materialize these into files before running. If it
# simply passes one filename, the first few FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() calls will
# iterate different entries. We ensure all paths are unique and valid, and
# contents are valid-enough for OpenSSL/libmosquitto to parse in many cases.

PEM_LINE = b"-----\n"

# Minimal but valid-ish PEM blocks. Not cryptographically correct, but commonly
# accepted by parsers for structure-path coverage.

def pem_block(header: str, body_b64: bytes, footer: str) -> bytes:
    return (f"-----BEGIN {header}-----\n".encode() + body_b64 + b"\n" + f"-----END {footer}-----\n".encode())


def rand_b64(rng: random.Random, lines: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
    out = []
    for _ in range(lines):
        line = bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(64))
        out.append(line + b"\n")
    return b"".join(out)


def make_ca_cert(rng: random.Random, chain: bool) -> bytes:
    # Create one or two certs in a single PEM file if chain=True
    lines = rng.randint(8, 24)
    cert1 = pem_block("CERTIFICATE", rand_b64(rng, lines), "CERTIFICATE")
    if chain:
        lines2 = rng.randint(8, 24)
        cert2 = pem_block("CERTIFICATE", rand_b64(rng, lines2), "CERTIFICATE")
        return cert1 + cert2
    return cert1


def make_client_cert(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return make_ca_cert(rng, chain=False)


def make_pkcs8_key(rng: random.Random, encrypted: bool) -> bytes:
    lines = rng.randint(8, 24)
    if encrypted:
        # Include Proc-Type and DEK-Info headers to mimic encrypted key
        header = (
            b"-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----\n" +
            rand_b64(rng, lines) +
            b"-----END ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
        )
        return header
    else:
        return pem_block("PRIVATE KEY", rand_b64(rng, lines), "PRIVATE KEY")


def make_traditional_rsa_key(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    lines = rng.randint(8, 24)
    return pem_block("RSA PRIVATE KEY", rand_b64(rng, lines), "RSA PRIVATE KEY")


def make_capath_dir_entries(rng: random.Random) -> List[Tuple[str, bytes]]:
    # Simulate hashed CA directory with files like abcd1234.0 containing a cert
    entries: List[Tuple[str, bytes]] = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for i in range(count):
        name = f"capath/{rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFF):x}.{i % 2}"
        content = make_ca_cert(rng, chain=False)
        entries.append((name, content))
    return entries


def add_entry(buf: bytearray, typ: int, path: str, content: bytes | None):
    path_b = path.encode()
    if len(path_b) > 1024:
        path_b = path_b[:1024]
    buf.extend(struct.pack("<4s" if False else ""))  # no-op placeholder
    buf.extend(b"")


def pack_entries(entries: List[Tuple[int, str, bytes | None]]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out.extend(b"MFS1")
    out.extend(struct.pack("<H", len(entries)))
    for typ, path, content in entries:
        path_b = path.encode()
        out.extend(struct.pack("<B", typ))
        out.extend(struct.pack("<H", len(path_b)))
        out.extend(path_b)
        if typ == 0:
            data = content or b""
            out.extend(struct.pack("<I", len(data)))
            out.extend(data)
        else:
            out.extend(struct.pack("<I", 0))
    return bytes(out)


def build_filesystem(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    entries: List[Tuple[int, str, bytes | None]] = []

    # Base directory for grouping
    entries.append((1, "", None))  # root placeholder
    entries.append((1, "capath", None))

    # CA file variations
    entries.append((0, "ca.pem", make_ca_cert(rng, chain=rng.choice([False, True]))))
    # Secondary CA to vary selection
    entries.append((0, "alt_ca.pem", make_ca_cert(rng, chain=False)))

    # capath directory contents
    for name, content in make_capath_dir_entries(rng):
        entries.append((0, name, content))

    # Client cert and key variants
    entries.append((0, "client.crt", make_client_cert(rng)))

    if rng.choice([True, False]):
        entries.append((0, "client.key", make_pkcs8_key(rng, encrypted=rng.choice([False, True]))))
    else:
        entries.append((0, "client.key", make_traditional_rsa_key(rng)))

    # Some extra files to exercise different filenames (ignored or alternative picks)
    entries.append((0, "empty.pem", b""))
    entries.append((0, "garbage.txt", b"not a pem\n" * rng.randint(1, 8)))

    return pack_entries(entries)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build the pseudo-filesystem archive
    fs = build_filesystem(rng)

    # Limit total size to 4096 bytes: if oversized, trim low-value extras by
    # dropping garbage/empty first, otherwise truncate safely at end.
    if len(fs) > 4096:
        # Attempt a rebuild with fewer extras
        rng2 = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5_5A5A)
        entries: List[Tuple[int, str, bytes | None]] = []
        entries.append((1, "", None))
        entries.append((1, "capath", None))
        entries.append((0, "ca.pem", make_ca_cert(rng2, chain=False)))
        for name, content in make_capath_dir_entries(rng2)[:1]:
            entries.append((0, name, content))
        entries.append((0, "client.crt", make_client_cert(rng2)))
        entries.append((0, "client.key", make_pkcs8_key(rng2, encrypted=False)))
        fs = pack_entries(entries)
        if len(fs) > 4096:
            fs = fs[:4096]

    return fs

import random
import string

# This generator targets ASCII string inputs used by the fuzzer stubs for:
# - mosquittopp::tls_opts_set (tls_version, ciphers)
# - mosquittopp::tls_psk_set (identity, optional ciphers)
#
# The stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR for these fields and may truncate lengths.
# We produce a single buffer that concatenates multiple newline-separated
# candidate strings so the fuzzer can draw from rich, valid options.
#
# Strategy:
# - Include a mix of known-good TLS version tokens and plausible variants.
# - Include realistic cipher suite lists (OpenSSL-style names) and small
#   tokens as well as random ASCII strings of appropriate lengths.
# - Include valid UTF-8 identities of varying sizes, plus edge-case ASCII.
# - Keep everything printable ASCII and <= 4096 bytes total.
# - Randomized but seeded by input.
#
# Format of returned buffer:
#   The buffer is a UTF-8 bytes blob containing multiple lines. Each line is a
#   candidate ASCII string that the FUZZ_PARAM_STR provider can use. Many fuzz
#   harnesses consume the buffer sequentially or as a pool of strings.

_DEF_TLS_VERS = [
    "tlsv1", "tlsv1.0", "tlsv1.1", "tlsv1.2", "tlsv1.3",
    "TLSv1", "TLSv1.0", "TLSv1.1", "TLSv1.2", "TLSv1.3",
    # common aliases/variants
    "TLS1.2", "TLS1_2", "TLS1.3", "TLS1_3", "tls1.2", "tls1_2",
    # minimal/empty-like but valid short tokens
    "TLS", "tls"
]

_DEF_CIPHERS = [
    # OpenSSL-style names
    "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
    "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
    "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
    "ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
    "AES128-GCM-SHA256",
    "AES256-GCM-SHA384",
    # Colon separated lists
    "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
    "ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:AES256-GCM-SHA384",
    # OpenSSL default-ish strings
    "DEFAULT:@SECLEVEL=1",
    "HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5",
    "HIGH:MEDIUM:!aNULL:!MD5:!RC4",
    # Short tokens
    "HIGH",
    "DEFAULT",
]

# Identity should be valid UTF-8 ASCII; include typical usernames and edge cases
_DEF_IDENTITIES = [
    "client", "user", "test", "tester", "fuzz", "mqtt", "device01",
    "id", "a", "Z", "client-123", "user_name", "user.name",
    "client/with/slash", "client+plus", "client=equals", "client@host",
]

_PRINTABLE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
_SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./@+ ="


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, charset: str = _SAFE_ASCII) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(charset) for _ in range(n))


def _build_tls_versions(rng: random.Random) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    # Always include known tokens
    out.extend(_DEF_TLS_VERS)
    # Add some plausible variants and random short tokens (<=8 as per stub truncation)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)):
        base = rng.choice(["tls", "TLS", "tlsv1", "TLSv1", "TLS1"]) 
        variant = rng.choice(["", ".0", ".1", ".2", ".3", "1.2", "1.3", "1_2", "1_3"])
        s = base + variant
        if len(s) > 8:
            s = s[:8]
        out.append(s)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)):
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8)
        out.append(s)
    return out


def _build_ciphers(rng: random.Random) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    out.extend(_DEF_CIPHERS)
    # Generate some random cipher list strings up to 32 chars (stub truncates to 32)
    tokens = [
        "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
        "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
        "AES128-GCM-SHA256",
        "AES256-GCM-SHA384",
        "CHACHA20-POLY1305",
        "HIGH", "DEFAULT", "MEDIUM",
        "@SECLEVEL=1", "@SECLEVEL=2",
    ]
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        parts = [rng.choice(tokens) for __ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
        s = ":".join(parts)
        if len(s) > 32:
            s = s[:32]
        out.append(s)
    # Add random ASCII ciphers strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 32)
        out.append(s)
    return out


def _build_identities(rng: random.Random) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    out.extend(_DEF_IDENTITIES)
    # Edge cases: empty not useful (must be non-NULL), but very short and max length 64
    out.append("x")
    out.append("0")
    # Generate varying length identities (1..64)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(10, 20)):
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64)
        out.append(s)
    # Structured identities
    for i in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        user = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12, string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-.")
        host = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12, string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-.")
        s = f"{user}@{host}"
        if len(s) > 64:
            s = s[:64]
        out.append(s)
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    tls_versions = _build_tls_versions(rng)
    ciphers = _build_ciphers(rng)
    identities = _build_identities(rng)

    # Interleave lines so early consumption gets a mixture
    lines: list[str] = []
    # Include headers to hint at semantic grouping (still valid ASCII inputs)
    lines.append("# TLS Versions")
    lines.extend(tls_versions)
    lines.append("# Cipher Lists")
    lines.extend(ciphers)
    lines.append("# Identities")
    lines.extend(identities)

    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes. If exceeded, trim lines from the end.
    encoded_lines = []
    total = 0
    for s in lines:
        b = (s + "\n").encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        if total + len(b) > 4096:
            break
        encoded_lines.append(b)
        total += len(b)

    return b"".join(encoded_lines)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: hex string (lowercase), even length, no 0x prefix.
# This generator aims to produce valid buffers that the fuzzer stub will
# interpret via FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME etc. In this stub,
# the interesting piece is a PSK hex string (even length, 2..64 chars),
# plus related UTF-8 identity/cipher strings. We pack multiple components
# into one bytes buffer separated by newlines so the harness can draw
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR values from it sequentially.
#
# Layout we generate (all ASCII, UTF-8 safe):
#   line1: PSK hex (2..64 chars, even length)
#   line2: identity string (UTF-8, up to 64 bytes) – non-empty typical, but allow empty
#   line3: optional ciphers string (up to 32 bytes); may be empty to simulate NULL in stub
# Additional trailing data may exist; consumers typically read sequentially.

HEX = '0123456789abcdef'

IDENTITY_SET = (
    ["client", "user", "identity", "id", "mqtt", "device", "sensor"]
    + [f"user{i}" for i in range(10)]
    + ["α", "β", "γ", "测试", "тест", "ユーザ", "utilisateur"]  # ensure UTF-8 diversity
)

CIPHERS_EXAMPLES = [
    "",  # allow empty -> caller may choose to ignore or treat as NULL
    "PSK-AES128-CBC-SHA",
    "PSK-AES256-CBC-SHA",
    "PSK-CHACHA20-POLY1305",
    "TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256",
    "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384",
]

def _rand_even_len_hex(rng: random.Random, min_hex: int = 2, max_hex: int = 64) -> str:
    # ensure even length
    if min_hex % 2 == 1:
        min_hex += 1
    if max_hex % 2 == 1:
        max_hex -= 1
    # choose a number of bytes 1..32 -> 2..64 hex chars
    nbytes = rng.randint(1, 32)
    length = max(min(nbytes * 2, max_hex), min_hex)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(HEX) for _ in range(length))


def _rand_identity(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct identities that are valid UTF-8 and within 64 bytes.
    base = rng.choice(IDENTITY_SET)
    # Optionally add a suffix to diversify while staying within 64 bytes.
    suffix = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        suffix = f"-{rng.randint(0, 9999)}"
    ident = (base + suffix)[:64]
    return ident


def _rand_ciphers(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Frequently empty to let stub optionally pass NULL or a short string
        return rng.choice(CIPHERS_EXAMPLES)
    # Otherwise generate a custom token-like cipher list within 32 chars
    tokens = [
        "PSK", "AES128", "AES256", "GCM", "SHA256", "SHA384", "CHACHA20", "POLY1305"
    ]
    parts: List[str] = []
    while parts and len('-'.join(parts)) < 8 and rng.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(rng.choice(tokens))
    if not parts:
        parts = [rng.choice(tokens), rng.choice(tokens)]
    s = '-'.join(parts)
    return s[:32]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    psk = _rand_even_len_hex(rng)
    identity = _rand_identity(rng)
    ciphers = _rand_ciphers(rng)

    # Assemble lines, ensure total <= 4096 bytes
    lines = [psk, identity, ciphers]
    data = ('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import ipaddress
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: hostname
# We want to generate valid, interesting host strings suitable for SOCKS5 host parameter,
# plus optional username/password strings if the fuzzer reuses the same buffer. The fuzzer
# uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() multiple times; our single bytes buffer will be split by the harness.
# Common convention is to provide multiple NUL-terminated or newline-separated strings.
# We'll generate a sequence of length-prefixed segments so arbitrary parsers can extract
# multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR values deterministically. Each segment: [1 byte type][2 bytes len][data]
# Types help provide variety for host/username/password consumers.
# Total size <= 4096 bytes.

# Segment types:
# 0: hostname (DNS label)
# 1: IPv4 literal
# 2: IPv6 literal
# 3: punycode-like unicode hostname (valid UTF-8)
# 4: short keyword host (localhost)
# 5: empty (consumer should replace with default)
# 6: long but within 128 limit host
# 7: username
# 8: password
# 9: numeric-only label

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

RFC_LABEL_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"


def _dns_label(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=63) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure starts and ends with alnum per DNS label rules
    if L == 1:
        return rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    inner_len = max(0, L - 2)
    inner = ''.join(rng.choice(RFC_LABEL_CHARS) for _ in range(inner_len))
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    end = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    return start + inner + end


def _dns_name(rng: random.Random, labels: int | None = None) -> str:
    if labels is None:
        labels = rng.randint(2, 5)
    parts = []
    for i in range(labels):
        parts.append(_dns_label(rng))
    return '.'.join(parts)


def _ipv4(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include edge and private ranges
    choices = [
        (0, 0, 0, 0), (255, 255, 255, 255), (127, 0, 0, 1), (224, 0, 0, 1),
        (10, 0, 0, 1), (172, 16, 0, 1), (192, 168, 1, 1)
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        a, b, c, d = rng.choice(choices)
    else:
        a = rng.randint(0, 255)
        b = rng.randint(0, 255)
        c = rng.randint(0, 255)
        d = rng.randint(0, 255)
    return f"{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}"


def _ipv6(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate variety: full, compressed, loopback, v4-mapped
    r = rng.random()
    if r < 0.25:
        return "::1"
    elif r < 0.5:
        # compressed random
        hextets = [rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF) for _ in range(8)]
        # pick a run to compress
        start = rng.randint(0, 7)
        end = rng.randint(start, 7)
        # ensure at least one zero in the run
        for i in range(start, end + 1):
            hextets[i] = 0
        # build with :: once
        parts: List[str] = []
        i = 0
        used = False
        while i < 8:
            if hextets[i] == 0:
                if not used:
                    parts.append("")
                    used = True
                while i < 8 and hextets[i] == 0:
                    i += 1
                if i == 8:
                    parts.append("")
                    break
                parts.append("")
            else:
                parts.append(format(hextets[i], 'x'))
                i += 1
        txt = ':'.join(parts)
        txt = txt.replace(':::', '::')
        if not txt.startswith('::') and '::' not in txt:
            # fallback ensure compression
            txt = ':'.join(format(h, 'x') for h in hextets)
        return txt
    elif r < 0.75:
        # full form
        return ':'.join(format(rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF), 'x') for _ in range(8))
    else:
        # v4-mapped
        return f"::ffff:{_ipv4(rng)}"


def _unicode_hostname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build labels from a limited safe subset of unicode letters keeping valid UTF-8
    # Use some non-ASCII like Greek, Cyrillic, CJK.
    greek = [chr(c) for c in range(0x03B1, 0x03C9 + 1)]  # alpha..omega
    cyr = [chr(c) for c in range(0x0430, 0x044F + 1)]    # a..ya
    kana = [chr(c) for c in range(0x3041, 0x3096 + 1)]   # hiragana
    pool = greek + cyr + kana + list(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + '-_')
    labels = rng.randint(2, 3)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(labels):
        L = rng.randint(1, 10)
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(L))
        # ensure not empty and doesn't start/end with hyphen
        if s[0] == '-':
            s = 'a' + s[1:]
        if s[-1] == '-':
            s = s[:-1] + 'z'
        parts.append(s)
    return '.'.join(parts)


def _long_host(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct close to 128 chars overall (fuzzer truncates to 128)
    parts = []
    while True:
        parts.append(_dns_label(rng, min_len=1, max_len=20))
        name = '.'.join(parts)
        if len(name) >= 120:
            break
    return name[:128]


def _username(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common username patterns
    choices = [
        'user', 'admin', 'test', 'guest',
        'user' + str(rng.randint(1, 9999)),
        'u_' + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '._-') for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 16)))
    ]
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _password(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of simple and complex
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return 'password'
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation
    return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(rng.randint(6, 32)))


def _encode_segment(seg_type: int, data: str) -> bytes:
    b = data.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    ln = len(b)
    if ln > 65535:
        b = b[:65535]
        ln = len(b)
    return bytes([seg_type & 0xFF]) + ln.to_bytes(2, 'big') + b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    segments: List[bytes] = []

    # Always include a primary host candidate first
    host_generators = [
        (0, lambda: _dns_name(rng)),
        (1, lambda: _ipv4(rng)),
        (2, lambda: _ipv6(rng)),
        (3, lambda: _unicode_hostname(rng)),
        (4, lambda: 'localhost'),
        (5, lambda: ''),  # empty to trigger defaulting in stub
        (6, lambda: _long_host(rng)),
        (9, lambda: str(rng.randint(0, 10**12)))
    ]

    # Pick 1-3 host variants to provide diverse FUZZ_PARAM_STR returns
    host_count = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(host_count):
        t, fn = rng.choice(host_generators)
        segments.append(_encode_segment(t, fn()))

    # Also provide typical username/password pairs so that when the fuzzer decides to use them,
    # it has meaningful data capped at 64 bytes (the stub truncates to 64).
    # Include multiple options to exercise NULL/with-credentials logic.
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        segments.append(_encode_segment(7, _username(rng)))
        segments.append(_encode_segment(8, _password(rng)))

    # Cap total size
    blob = b''.join(segments)
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        blob = blob[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return blob
